output.summary: A palm-like, cone-bearing plant from seasonally dry tropical woodlands in northern Australia, Cycas media has thick, dark-green leaves that emerge in annual flushes. It often grows new foliage immediately after dry-season fires. All parts are considered highly toxic, but Aboriginal Australians ate the seeds after extensive toxin-removing preparation.
output.edibilityNote: Aboriginal Australians ate seeds only after extensive preparation, including pounding, drying, prolonged soaking, grinding and baking, to remove toxins.
